definition: The 10 mount / heavenly-being desertion cases of the Xiyouji world reveal 'huge sentencing disparities between demons with backing and without' — a core case of Xiyouji judicial sociology.

desertion_cases.name: Green Ox Demon
desertion_cases.owner_rank: One of the Three Pure Ones · the Daoist Patriarch
desertion_cases.descent_reason: A boy tended it carelessly · the Green Ox slipped down to the mortal realm while its pen was unlocked
crimes_committed: Stealing the Diamond Bracelet
Snatching the Golden-banded Staff and other treasures
Kidnapping Tang Sanzang
Battling the divine generals of Heaven
desertion_cases.final_outcome: The Supreme Lord Laozi personally descended to take it back · returned to the Tushita Palace
desertion_cases.legal_analysis: leniently handled by the owner · continued service after symbolic discipline · no substantive punishment

desertion_cases.name: Goldfish Demon
desertion_cases.owner_rank: Foremost of the four great bodhisattvas
desertion_cases.descent_reason: A goldfish in Guanyin's lotus pond · while Guanyin was away it surfaced to listen to sutras and became a spirit · then descended to wreak havoc
crimes_committed: Eating a boy and a girl each year at the Tongtian River
Kidnapping Tang Sanzang
Freezing the Tongtian River to trap the pilgrims
desertion_cases.final_outcome: Guanyin collected it in a bamboo basket and returned it to the lotus pond
desertion_cases.legal_analysis: taken back by the owner · no punishment · merely returned to its post

desertion_cases.name: Golden-haired Hou
desertion_cases.owner_rank: Foremost of the four great bodhisattvas
desertion_cases.descent_reason: The herder fell asleep · the Golden-haired Hou bit through its tether and escaped to the mortal realm
crimes_committed: Abducting the queen of Zhuzi Kingdom
Kidnapping Tang Sanzang
Threatening with the Purple-gold Bell magic
desertion_cases.final_outcome: Guanyin personally took it back · returned to the South Sea
desertion_cases.legal_analysis: taken back by the owner · no punishment · the queen of Zhuzi was returned

desertion_cases.name: Green-maned Lion Demon
desertion_cases.owner_rank: One of the four great bodhisattvas
desertion_cases.descent_reason: Manjushri's mount · descended to Wuji Kingdom · punished the king by the Buddha's decree (pushed him into a well and drowned for three days)
crimes_committed: Usurping the throne of Wuji Kingdom
Impersonating the king for three years
Pushing the king into a well to drown (later revived)
desertion_cases.final_outcome: Manjushri took it back · returned to Mount Wutai
desertion_cases.legal_analysis: taken back by the owner · no punishment · nominally 'retribution by Buddha's decree'

desertion_cases.name: Yellow-tusked Elephant
desertion_cases.owner_rank: One of the four great bodhisattvas
desertion_cases.descent_reason: Samantabhadra's mount · descended to Lion-Camel Ridge as the second demon king
crimes_committed: Devouring countless people at Lion-Camel Ridge
Kidnapping Tang Sanzang
Allying with Green Lion and Dapeng to besiege
desertion_cases.final_outcome: Samantabhadra took it back · returned to Mount Emei
desertion_cases.legal_analysis: taken back by the owner · no substantive punishment · despite a long list of crimes

desertion_cases.name: Golden-winged Dapeng
desertion_cases.owner_rank: The Buddha himself · brother of the Peacock Mahāmāyūrī Bodhisattva
desertion_cases.descent_reason: Brother of the Peacock Mahāmāyūrī Bodhisattva · a relative of the Buddha's mother · descended to the kingdom of Lion-Camel as the third demon king
crimes_committed: Destroying the kingdom of Lion-Camel and eating all its people
Kidnapping Tang Sanzang
Resisting Tathāgata in person
Threatening with the Yin-Yang Two-Energy Bottle
desertion_cases.final_outcome: Tathāgata came in person to subdue it · appointed it a Dharma protector · kept at Spirit Mountain
desertion_cases.legal_analysis: despite heinous crimes, spared due to kinship with the Buddha · even appointed a Dharma protector · a 'get-out-of-punishment pass for the privileged class'

desertion_cases.name: Nine-spirit Sage
desertion_cases.owner_rank: The Great Emperor of the Eastern Azure Splendor · one of the Four Daoist Sovereigns
desertion_cases.descent_reason: Mount of the Great Emperor Taiyi · descended to Zhujie Mountain as a nine-headed lion
crimes_committed: Dominating a region from the Nine-twists Cave
Subduing the Yellow Lion and six lion descendants
Kidnapping Tang Sanzang and his disciples
desertion_cases.final_outcome: The Great Emperor Taiyi personally took it back · returned to the Eastern Miraculous Rock Palace
desertion_cases.legal_analysis: taken back by the owner · no punishment · though it didn't eat people, its sphere of influence was large

desertion_cases.name: Yellow Robe Demon
desertion_cases.owner_rank: A star officer of the Heavenly Court · not a mount but a control case of a heavenly being descending
desertion_cases.descent_reason: Kuimulang and the Jade Maiden of Poxiang Hall had a secret affair · agreed to descend and continue their romance
crimes_committed: Forcibly abducting Princess Baihuaxiu of Precious Elephant Kingdom
Usurping the son-in-law's position
Eating palace maids
Forcing Tang Sanzang to turn into a tiger
desertion_cases.final_outcome: Recalled by the Heavenly Court · demoted to stoke fires at the Tushita Palace · later reinstated
desertion_cases.legal_analysis: a heavenly being's descent drew heavier punishment · demoted to stoke fires · but ultimately reinstated · still lenient compared to the light punishment of mounts

desertion_cases.name: White Elephant
desertion_cases.owner_rank: One of the four great bodhisattvas
desertion_cases.descent_reason: Samantabhadra's mount · descended to Lion-Camel Ridge as the second demon king · allied with Green Lion and Dapeng
crimes_committed: Devouring countless people at Lion-Camel Ridge
Kidnapping Tang Sanzang
Wrapping its trunk around Wukong, nearly killing him
desertion_cases.final_outcome: Samantabhadra took it back · returned to Mount Emei
desertion_cases.legal_analysis: same type of incident as the Yellow-tusked Elephant · taken back by the owner · no substantive punishment

desertion_cases.name: Green Lion
desertion_cases.owner_rank: One of the four great bodhisattvas
desertion_cases.descent_reason: Manjushri's mount · descended to Lion-Camel Ridge as the chief demon king · allied with White Elephant and Dapeng
crimes_committed: Swallowing countless travelers at Lion-Camel Ridge
Kidnapping Tang Sanzang
Opening its mouth to swallow Wukong
desertion_cases.final_outcome: Manjushri took it back · returned to Mount Wutai
desertion_cases.legal_analysis: same type of incident as the Green-maned Lion Demon · taken back by the owner · no substantive punishment

desertion_stats.lowest_severity: Green Ox Demon / Goldfish Demon / Golden-haired Hou / Green-maned Lion Demon / Yellow-tusked Elephant / Nine-spirit Sage / White Elephant / Green Lion (all 2–3)
desertion_stats.verdict_pattern: taken back by owner in 8 cases · demoted in 1 · promoted in 1 · 0% actual punishment rate
desertion_stats.legal_bias: 100% of mount-desertion cases were never executed · revealing '100% sentencing immunity for demons with backing'
comparable_wild_demons: White Bone Demon beaten to death
Three demons of Chechi Kingdom died miserably

desertion_insights: 0 of the 10 mount-desertion cases were executed · versus 60%+ wild-demon mortality · blatant judicial double standards
Guanyin / Manjushri / Samantabhadra together account for 6 cases · revealing 'bodhisattva mounts are the main force of descents'

Though the Golden-winged Dapeng committed heinous crimes (wiping out the kingdom of Lion-Camel), it was instead appointed a Dharma protector due to kinship with the Buddha — an extreme case of privileged justice
The Yellow Robe Demon, as a descending heavenly being, drew relatively heavier punishment (demoted to stoke fires) · showing Heavenly Court justice is slightly stricter than the Buddhist realm
The three demons of Lion-Camel Ridge (Green Lion / White Elephant / Dapeng) are a classic case of gang-style mount desertion · the three owners cooperatively took them back
The 'dereliction of duty' in mount desertions should punish the owners · but in Journey to the West no owner bears substantive responsibility · revealing 'the absence of regulatory accountability'
average sentence severity only 2.8/10 · severely mismatched with the seriousness of the crimes · the core contradiction of Xiyouji judicial sociology
